chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Ibn Mukkan from al-Halabi and Ibn Abi Umayr and Hammad from al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has dinars upon him (as debt or possession), so he said: 'There is no harm in him taking their price in dirhams.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell gold dinars for silver dirhams to pay off a debt in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of exchanging gold dinars for silver dirhams to settle debts, affirming that such a transaction is valid (*la ba'sa*) even if the weights differ, provided the price is agreed upon. It reflects the Shia juristic view that this exchange falls under *bay' al-sarf* (currency exchange) rather than *riba al-fadl* (excess in same-kind exchange), as long as the transaction is not deferred. The narration, transmitted through a chain including Safwan and Ibn Muskan, underscores the practical application of these rules in commercial contexts during the Imams' era.
